name: imperial-units

description.en: Imperial and US customary units in 33 cards: length, area, volume, mass, speed, pressure, power, energy and the Fahrenheit formulas, with the nautical mile and knot as common non-SI extras. The front names a unit, keeping US and imperial versions apart where they differ; the back gives its value in SI units or litres with a decimal point, exact where the definition is exact and short, otherwise rounded to four significant digits and marked ≈. Compiled from NIST Handbook 44 (2026) and NIST SP 811, checked against the UK Weights and Measures Act 1985 and Wikidata.

method: Who did the work: Anton Wiklund compiled this deck with the help of AI agents (Claude, by Anthropic), which did the research, drafting and cross-checking at his direction. The cards were checked by machine (an exact-arithmetic Python script, live Wikidata and the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators) and in independent review rounds by further Claude agents, each logged under Quality control with its findings and how they were resolved. Anton Wiklund reviews every deck in full before it is released.

Sources: downloaded Appendix C (General Tables of Units of Measurement) and the title page of NIST Handbook 44, 2026 edition (approved December 2025, the current edition on NIST's Handbook 44 page on 2026-10-04), NIST Special Publication 811 (2008) with its Appendix B conversion factors, NIST's licensing statements, and the revised text of Schedule 1 of the UK Weights and Measures Act 1985 (legislation.gov.uk XML), and extracted their text with pypdf and Beautiful Soup (see Queries). SP 811 marks exact factors in bold; since bold does not survive text extraction, the fonts of the factor columns were read with pdfplumber (bold.py).

Selection: started from the units the brief named and the units HB 44's Tables of Equivalents and the British notes cover, and kept those in everyday or technical use today: the length units from the inch to the mile plus the fathom, chain and furlong; the square foot, acre and square mile; the cubic foot, the US and imperial gallon, liquid pint and fluid ounce, and the 42-gallon oil barrel; the grain, avoirdupois ounce, troy ounce, pound, stone, short ton and long ton; the mile per hour; the psi, mechanical horsepower and International Table Btu; and the two Fahrenheit conversion formulas. The nautical mile and the knot are not imperial or US customary units but SI-accepted non-SI units; they were kept because they are common, and their notes say so.

Values: every value comes from the NIST sources. Where HB 44 gives an exact value (marked "(exactly)" in its Tables of Equivalents, or the full-precision entries of its Section 4 conversion tables, whose exact figures the PDF underlines; the underlining does not survive text extraction, so each such value was recomputed by verify.py), that value is used; the imperial gallon (4.546 09 L) is exact in SP 811 (bold), and the imperial pint, imperial fluid ounce, stone and long ton follow from it and from the pound by the relations in HB 44's Notes on British Units (8 pints and 160 fluid ounces to the gallon, 14 pounds to the stone, 2240 pounds to the ton). The Btu (IT) and the pound-force are exact in SP 811's notes 9 and 23; the psi and horsepower are derived from the pound-force (verify.py), and NIST's rounded values (6894.757 Pa, 745.6999 W) were compared with them. All values use the international foot (HB 44 2026: the US survey foot was deprecated at the end of 2022).

Card text: the front names one unit, "1 inch (in)" / "1 tum (in)", with its usual symbol where NIST gives one and with "US" or "imperial" (Swedish "amerikansk", "brittisk (imperial)") wherever the US and British units differ. The back is the value in SI units or, for volumes, in litres (L, mL), a non-SI unit accepted for use with the SI (SP 811 Table 6), written without a language (zxx) with a decimal point: the exact value when it has at most 8 significant digits, otherwise rounded to 4 significant digits and marked "≈", in which case the note gives the exact value (or NIST's 7-digit value for the psi and horsepower). The unit on the back is chosen for readability (cm for the inch, mL for fluid ounces, g for ounces, L for volumes, km² for the square mile). The two temperature cards give NIST's formulas with 1.8; notes add 5/9 and check points. English and Swedish notes give the defining relation (12 inches, 14 pounds ...) and, for the US and imperial pairs, the difference.

Verification of every value: verify.py recomputes all 31 numerical cards with Python's exact fractions from the base definitions (inch 0.0254 m, pound 0.453 592 37 kg, US gallon 231 in³, imperial gallon 4.546 09 L, standard gravity 9.806 65 m/s², Btu 1055.055 852 62 J), applies the rounding rule above, asserts the derived values against HB 44's exact table entries and the UK Act's own figures (pint 0.568 261 25 dm³, acre 4840 yd², chain 22 yd ...), and checks that the two Fahrenheit formulas are inverse and map 32 °F to 0 °C, 212 °F to 100 °C, −40 °C to −40 °F and −459.67 °F to −273.15 °C. Every card's back was compared with the script's output.

Second source: each card is backed by both NIST publications where both list the unit, and checked against the UK Act wherever UK law defines it (verification only, see Licensing), against Wikidata (labels, symbols and the conversion to SI unit, P2370, via the builder's machine checks) and against the Swedish Wikipedia article on the unit. Wikidata's value is checked wherever it is the exact value or a correct rounding of it to at least the precision the card's back shows (rounded values checked: US gallon, US liquid pint, US and imperial fluid ounce, oil barrel, psi, horsepower, Btu; p2370.py compares each with the exact value). It is left out where it is wrong (imperial gallon), coarser than the card (knot, 0.514 m/s) or on a generic item with the old US survey value (fathom and chain, which are checked on the international items instead); each difference is recorded under Quality control (rounds 0 and 3). No check was dropped to make the build pass.

Swedish: unit names are Wikidata's Swedish labels where they exist and match Swedish usage (tum, fot, yard, engelsk mil, nautisk mil, famn, chain, furlong, kvadratfot, kubikfot, uns, grain, short ton, knop, psi), and otherwise the plain Swedish descriptive forms confirmed by the Swedish Wikipedia articles: amerikansk/brittisk gallon and pint ("gallon (USA, våt)", "imperial gallon (Storbritannien)"), troy-uns, pund (Wikidata's 'skålpund' is an old Swedish unit), engelskt ton (long ton), brittisk hästkraft (Swedish hk normally means the metric horsepower), fat for the oil barrel, acre. "Engelsk kvadratmil" is our own form, parallel to "engelsk mil" and kept apart from the Swedish mil. Swedish notes use the decimal comma, the litre symbols l and ml, and uninflected plurals after numbers ("10 chain", "160 brittiska fluid ounce"); fluid ounce is neuter ("ett fluid ounce", Swedish Wikipedia). The backs, which have no language, use the decimal point and L/mL.

Left out (see Selection): units that are rare today or ambiguous without context (rod, link, league, cable, hand, gill, dram, minim, pennyweight, apothecaries' units, peck, bushel, quart, hundredweight, US cup, tablespoon and teaspoon, which have several legal definitions), the US survey versions of the foot, acre and chain, the US dry pint (mentioned in a note), and compound units other than the mile per hour, the knot and the psi.
selection: 33 cards: 29 imperial and US customary units of length (inch, foot, yard, mile, fathom, chain, furlong), area (square foot, acre, square mile), volume (cubic foot; US and imperial gallon, liquid pint and fluid ounce; the 42-gallon oil barrel), mass (grain, avoirdupois ounce, troy ounce, pound, stone, short ton, long ton), speed (mile per hour), pressure (psi), power (mechanical horsepower) and energy (International Table Btu), the nautical mile and the knot as common non-SI units outside the imperial and US systems, and the two Fahrenheit–Celsius conversion formulas. US and imperial units are separate cards wherever they differ (gallon, pint, fluid ounce, short and long ton). Every value uses the international foot and pound of 1959; the US survey foot and the units defined from it are left out because NIST deprecated it at the end of 2022. Left out as rare or with several competing definitions: rod, link, league, cable, hand, gill, dram, minim, pennyweight, the apothecaries' units, peck, bushel, quart, hundredweight, cup, tablespoon and teaspoon, the dry pint (in a note only) and the other barrels (31-gallon beer barrel in a note). Values follow the NIST Handbook 44 (2026) and SP 811 as of 2026-10-04; the yard and pound have been the international ones since 1959, and the imperial gallon is exactly 4.546 09 L (SP 811; UK law).

"""Extract text from the downloaded PDFs and HTML/XML pages (run with uv run --with pypdf --with beautifulsoup4)."""
import os
import pypdf
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup

d = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)) + "/"
for n in ["hb44-2026-appendix-c", "hb44-2026-title-page", "nist-sp811-2008"]:
    r = pypdf.PdfReader(d + n + ".pdf")
    open(d + n + ".txt", "w", encoding="utf-8").write(
        "\n".join(f"=====PAGE {i+1}=====\n" + (p.extract_text() or "") for i, p in enumerate(r.pages)))
for n, ext, parser in [("nist-copyright", "html", "html.parser"), ("nist-techseries-licence", "html", "html.parser"),
                       ("legislation-copyright", "html", "html.parser"), ("wma1985-schedule1", "xml", "html.parser")]:
    s = BeautifulSoup(open(d + n + "." + ext, encoding="utf-8").read(), parser)
    for t in s(["script", "style", "noscript"]):
        t.decompose()
    open(d + n + ".txt", "w", encoding="utf-8").write(s.get_text("\n", strip=True))
print("ok")

"""Derive every card's SI value with exact rational arithmetic from the defining relations
(NIST HB 44 Appendix C, NIST SP 811 Appendix B, UK Weights and Measures Act 1985 Schedule 1),
and print the value as the card shows it: exact when it has at most 8 significant digits,
otherwise rounded to 4 significant digits with "≈". Usage: python3 verify.py"""
from fractions import Fraction as F
from decimal import Decimal, getcontext

getcontext().prec = 40
INCH = F(254, 10000)               # m, 1959 agreement (HB 44 C-9 note; SP 811 B.8, bold)
FOOT = 12 * INCH                   # HB 44 C-5: 12 inches = 1 foot
YARD = 3 * FOOT                    # HB 44 C-5: 3 feet = 1 yard; UK Act: yard = 0.9144 m
MILE = 5280 * FOOT                 # HB 44 C-5
NMI = F(1852)                      # HB 44 C-22, SP 811 (bold)
FATHOM = 6 * FOOT                  # HB 44 C-5
CHAIN = 66 * FOOT                  # HB 44 C-5; UK Act: 22 yards
FURLONG = 660 * FOOT               # HB 44 C-5; UK Act: 220 yards
SQFT = FOOT ** 2
ACRE = 43560 * SQFT                # HB 44 C-6; UK Act: 4840 square yards
SQMI = MILE ** 2                   # HB 44 C-6: 640 acres
CUFT = FOOT ** 3
LITRE = F(1, 1000)                 # m3
US_GAL = 231 * INCH ** 3           # HB 44 C-6: gallon = 231 cubic inches
IMP_GAL = F(454609, 100000) * LITRE  # SP 811 B.8 (bold, exact); UK Act: 4.54609 dm3
US_PINT = US_GAL / 8               # HB 44 C-6
IMP_PINT = IMP_GAL / 8             # HB 44 C-8 British table; UK Act Pt IV: 0.568 261 25 dm3
US_FLOZ = US_GAL / 128             # HB 44 C-6
IMP_FLOZ = IMP_GAL / 160           # HB 44 C-8; UK Act: 1/20 pint
BARREL = 42 * US_GAL               # HB 44 C-24 note 22; SP 811 B.8
POUND = F(45359237, 100000000)     # kg, SP 811 note 22; HB 44 C-17; UK Act
GRAIN = POUND / 7000               # HB 44 C-7
OUNCE = POUND / 16                 # HB 44 C-7
TROY_OZ = 480 * GRAIN              # HB 44 C-7
STONE = 14 * POUND                 # HB 44 C-8; UK Act
SHORT_TON = 2000 * POUND           # HB 44 C-7
LONG_TON = 2240 * POUND            # HB 44 C-7, C-8
MPH = MILE / 3600                  # m/s
KNOT = NMI / 3600                  # m/s
GN = F(980665, 100000)             # standard acceleration of gravity, SP 811
LBF = POUND * GN                   # N, SP 811 note 23
PSI = LBF / INCH ** 2              # Pa
HP = 550 * FOOT * LBF              # W, 550 ft·lbf/s
BTU_IT = F(105505585262, 100000000)  # J, SP 811 note 9: 1.055 055 852 62 kJ

CARDS = [
    ("inch", INCH, F(1, 100), "cm"), ("foot", FOOT, 1, "m"), ("yard", YARD, 1, "m"), ("mile", MILE, 1, "m"),
    ("nautical-mile", NMI, 1, "m"), ("fathom", FATHOM, 1, "m"), ("chain", CHAIN, 1, "m"), ("furlong", FURLONG, 1, "m"),
    ("square-foot", SQFT, 1, "m²"), ("acre", ACRE, 1, "m²"), ("square-mile", SQMI, 10 ** 6, "km²"),
    ("cubic-foot", CUFT, LITRE, "L"), ("us-gallon", US_GAL, LITRE, "L"), ("imperial-gallon", IMP_GAL, LITRE, "L"),
    ("us-pint", US_PINT, LITRE, "L"), ("imperial-pint", IMP_PINT, LITRE, "L"),
    ("us-fluid-ounce", US_FLOZ, LITRE / 1000, "mL"), ("imperial-fluid-ounce", IMP_FLOZ, LITRE / 1000, "mL"),
    ("oil-barrel", BARREL, LITRE, "L"), ("grain", GRAIN, F(1, 10 ** 6), "mg"), ("ounce", OUNCE, F(1, 1000), "g"),
    ("troy-ounce", TROY_OZ, F(1, 1000), "g"), ("pound", POUND, 1, "kg"), ("stone", STONE, 1, "kg"),
    ("short-ton", SHORT_TON, 1, "kg"), ("long-ton", LONG_TON, 1, "kg"), ("mile-per-hour", MPH, 1, "m/s"),
    ("knot", KNOT, 1, "m/s"), ("psi", PSI, 1, "Pa"), ("horsepower", HP, 1, "W"), ("btu", BTU_IT, 1, "J"),
]


def exact_decimal(x: F) -> str | None:
    d = x.denominator
    for p in (2, 5):
        while d % p == 0:
            d //= p
    if d != 1:
        return None
    s = format(Decimal(x.numerator) / Decimal(x.denominator), "f")
    return s.rstrip("0").rstrip(".") if "." in s else s


def sig_digits(s: str) -> int:
    return len(s.replace(".", "").lstrip("0"))


def show(x: F) -> str:
    e = exact_decimal(x)
    if e is not None and sig_digits(e) <= 8:
        return e
    v = Decimal(x.numerator) / Decimal(x.denominator)
    r = format(float(f"{v:.4g}"), "f") if v >= 1000 else f"{v:.{max(0, 3 - v.adjusted())}f}"
    if v >= 1000:
        r = str(int(float(f"{v:.4g}")))
